claimed_invariant: One execution produces ordered evaluated content with origins. Identity preserves every evaluated plain line (including sprites, blanks and boundaries), while parser lowering consumes sprites and lowers theme/option events without reevaluating TIM or changing its state.
causal_divergence: The integrated code reconstructs themed identity from raw input and replays theme bodies, including subblocks, in separate orders; non-themed identity creates another context. Sprites are erased before identity, user subblocks never execute, diagnostic comments are synthesized, inactive theme/option placeholders are discarded, raw initial blanks are dropped, and trailing apostrophes are incorrectly treated as TIM comments. Theme names never execute functions/variables. These are alternative projections/evaluation orders rather than Java resultList semantics.
planned_model_change: Replace dual passes and raw substitution with typed evaluated events: plain located text, boundaries, parser-only consumed directives/options and nested theme expansions. Evaluate each theme/sub/procedure once in the active memory; lower that same stream into identity and parser representation. Move sprite extraction to parser projection. Retain original line origins across consumed directives. Mirror Java comment iterator/inner-comment operations and retain blank lines. Resolve theme selectors (and local from expressions) before loading; inactive includes/themes must have no execution side effects.

boundary: No parse dispatcher, renderer, comparator or baseline changes. Sequence dispatcher may request a separate preprocessing operation; each returned representation must be internally single-evaluation. A cache across parse calls is not introduced.
